about: The one config file. Edit it by hand. 'fields': the fields each source document needs, per source name (10-K, 10-Q, press release ...); made once from the team's Information_Extraction_List.xlsx. Every field listed there needs a rule under 'rules' with the same name (any capital letters), otherwise it is reported as not found ('no extraction rule for this field'). The rest: How documents are recognised and how each field of 'fields' is filled. 'document_types': in order, each type's 'name' (the form reported in the metadata), 'cover' (the fixed sentence only its SEC cover page prints, searched on the first 'cover_pages' pages and winning over everything else), 'names' (a pattern searched on the first two pages when no cover sentence is found; the first type that matches wins) and 'field_lists' (the lists of 'fields' it is checked against; none = the document is skipped). 'rules' maps a field name (any capital letters) to a list of rules tried in order; the first that finds something fills the field ('note' on a rule is written to the metadata when that rule is used; 'forms' limits a rule to those document types). A field without a rule is reported as not found with the note 'no extraction rule for this field'. Patterns are Python regular expressions, matched without regard to capital letters. Rule kinds: rows (statement rows: 'parts' are standard row names from pdf_pipeline/statements.py FIELDS, or {statement, labels} for any row whose label matches), tables (tables with row_any / row_all / min_rows / mentions; only_rows keeps the matching rows), table_rows (single table rows whose label starts with 'pattern', in tables whose title matches 'title' when given), sentences (sentences matching 'pattern', at most 'limit', only on the pages of 'pages' or only inside the section under the heading 'section' when given, never on the 'skip_pages' scope), item (an Item's text, per form), note (the first note whose title matches), item1_part (a sub-section of Item 1 whose heading matches), section (the section under the first heading anywhere that matches 'heading'), audit_part (part of the audit report between 'start' and 'end'), not_in_filing (never in one document). 'page_scopes' name page ranges used by sentences: each is the union of notes (by title), Items (per form) and headed sections (by heading). 'applies_if' maps a field name to a pattern: when the field is not found and the pattern is not on the document's first two pages, the field is reported as not applicable (e.g. GE Vernova's own segments in another company's filing) instead of lowering the applicable score. Fields whose only rules are not_in_filing are reported as not applicable too.
